subject: python
title: Conditions
description: if / elif / else, comparison and boolean operators, and the traps around truthiness.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A condition chooses which block runs. Python tests the branches in order and runs the first one whose expression is true; elif branches are only reached when every branch above them was false.

content.title: Shape
content.body: The colon and the indentation are part of the syntax, not a style choice.

content.title: Good practice
content.body: Compare with == and assign with =. Chained comparisons such as 0 <= x <= 10 read better than combining two tests with and.

exercises.question: What does this print?
exercises.explanation: The first true branch wins and the rest are skipped. Order the widest condition last, or the A branch can never be reached.

exercises.question: Which line breaks this snippet?

answers.text: Line 3 — print must be indented by two spaces

exercises.explanation: = assigns, == compares. Python rejects assignment inside an if header with a SyntaxError.

exercises.question: Replacing elif with a second if can change which branches run.
exercises.explanation: Separate ifs are each tested independently, so two of them can both run. elif branches are mutually exclusive.

exercises.question: Complete the condition so it matches ages inside the range.
exercises.explanation: Both parts must hold, so the operator is and. Python spells the boolean operators as words: and, or, not.

exercises.question: Why is `if value is None` preferred over `if value == None`?

answers.text: is is faster, but otherwise identical
There is no difference; both are equally idiomatic
is compares identity, and None is a singleton — a custom __eq__ cannot fool it
== does not work with None at all

exercises.explanation: There is exactly one None object, so identity is the exact test. A class that overrides __eq__ could make == None return True by accident.

exercises.question: Complete the guard so the body runs only for non-empty lists.
exercises.explanation: An empty list is falsy, so `if not items` is the idiomatic early return. Python has no ! operator.

exercises.question: What is the value of the expression?
exercises.explanation: A chained comparison means 1 < x and x < 4. The second part is false for x = 5, so the whole thing is False.

exercises.question: Syntax
exercises.front: value = a if cond else b
exercises.back: The ternary form — one expression, evaluates only the branch it needs
exercises.explanation: Useful for short either/or assignments. Keep it to one line; nest it and readability drops fast.
